issues.legal_issue: The evidence did not establish a concluded sale agreement from the initial negotiations.
material_facts: The parties met to discuss a possible sale, but the seller said he still had to consult his brothers.
The later correspondence showed that the sale consideration had not been finalised and that further agreement was contemplated.
The plaintiff’s own notice acknowledged that consultation with the seller’s brothers was still required.
issues.conclusion: No concluded agreement was made at the initial meeting, so specific performance could not be granted on the basis of that alleged agreement.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit for specific performance, the agreement and its terms must be proved with absolute clarity and certainty. The Court relied on the principles governing the discretionary remedy under section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and on Madamsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yellogi Rao and Sardar Singh v. Smt. Krishna Devi.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged sale agreement.
predicates.seller_reserved_consultation: The seller said that he still needed to consult other owners before finalising the proposed sale.
predicates.later_correspondence_left_terms_unsettle: Correspondence after the meeting showed that material sale terms remained open for further discussion.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit rests on negotiations that left consultation or material terms unresolved, the alleged agreement is not treated as proved as a concluded agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff who declined an opportunity to amend the pleading could not obtain specific performance of a different agreement asserted later.
material_facts: The plaint sought specific performance of an agreement allegedly concluded at the initial meeting.
The High Court gave the plaintiff an opportunity to amend the plaint to claim specific performance of an agreement allegedly concluded at a later meeting.
The plaintiff declined that opportunity and argued in the Supreme Court for relief on the later alleged agreement.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff could not obtain relief for specific performance of the later alleged agreement after declining to amend the plaint to seek that relief.
issues.legal_principle: Specific performance must be sought on the agreement put in issue by the pleadings; a plaintiff cannot abandon the pleaded agreement and obtain a decree on a different agreement. The Court relied on the strict approach to variance in specific-performance suits described in Gonesh Ram v. Ganpat Rai, Md. Ziaul Haque v. Calcutta Vyapar Pratisthan, and Hawkins v. Maltby.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged agreement.
predicates.pleaded_agreement_differs_from_later_cla: The agreement identified in the pleading differed from the agreement later relied on for relief.
predicates.plaintiff_refused_amendment: The plaintiff declined an opportunity to amend the pleading to claim relief on the later alleged agreement.

issues.definition: In a specific-performance suit, when the pleaded agreement differs from the later claim and the plaintiff refuses an opportunity to amend, relief cannot be granted on the later agreement.

issues.legal_issue: In a specific-performance suit, general relief cannot support a decree based on a materially different agreement from the one pleaded and claimed.
material_facts: The plaint specifically alleged that the parties concluded an agreement at the initial meeting and sought specific performance of that agreement.
The plaint did not allege a separate concluded agreement at the later meeting; it described that meeting as involving arrangements for payment and execution.
The plaintiff relied on a general prayer for other relief to seek specific performance of the alleged later agreement.
There was no part performance by delivery of possession, and the difference between the pleaded and asserted agreements was not immaterial.
issues.conclusion: The general prayer could not support specific performance of the different agreement, even if evidence had established it.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 7 Rule 7 of the Code of Civil Procedure, general relief must be consistent with the pleaded and proved case and with the specific relief claimed. In specific-performance suits, the agreement to be enforced must conform to the pleadings and proof; a material variance is not cured by a general prayer. The Court relied on Gonesh Ram v. Ganpat Rai, Md. Ziaul Haque v. Calcutta Vyapar Pratisthan, Hawkins v. Maltby, Cargil v. Bower, and Kidar Lall Seal v. Hari Lall Seal.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and pleaded_agreement_differs_from_proved_agreement and no_part_performance and no_immaterial_variation and no_amendment

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged agreement.
predicates.pleaded_agreement_differs_from_proved_ag: The agreement described in the pleading differed materially from the agreement on which the evidence or later argument sought relief.
predicates.no_part_performance: The plaintiff had not partly performed the asserted agreement by taking possession of the property.
predicates.no_immaterial_variation: The difference between the pleaded agreement and the asserted agreement was material rather than insignificant.
predicates.no_amendment: The pleading was not amended to put the different agreement in issue.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim concerns an agreement materially different from the pleaded agreement, and there is no part performance, immaterial variation, or amendment, a general prayer does not permit a decree on that different agreement.

issues.legal_issue: The evidence did not establish a separate sale agreement at the later meeting.
material_facts: The plaintiff’s witness testified that no agreement was received at the later meeting.

The plaintiff testified that the seller asked him to return later, keep the consideration ready, and expected to execute a sale deed, but the evidence did not show that the parties negotiated and concluded a fresh agreement at that meeting.
The plaintiff’s evidence continued to assert that the agreement had been concluded at the initial meeting.
issues.conclusion: No fresh agreement was proved at the later meeting, and the evidence did not support specific performance on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: A specific-performance decree requires clear and certain proof of the agreement and its terms. The Court applied section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, and the principles on certainty and variance described in Gonesh Ram v. Ganpat Rai, Md. Ziaul Haque v. Calcutta Vyapar Pratisthan, and Hawkins v. Maltby.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an alleged agreement.
predicates.later_meeting_evidence_shows_only_future: Evidence of the later meeting showed requests to prepare for a future transaction rather than negotiations of a concluded sale.
predicates.no_fresh_terms_concluded: The evidence did not show that the parties settled and accepted the terms of a new agreement at the later meeting.

issues.definition: When evidence from a later meeting shows only arrangements for a future transaction and no settled terms, a separate agreement from that meeting is not proved.

issues.legal_issue: The appellate court’s refusal of specific performance did not warrant interference where its exercise of discretion followed established principles and was not perverse.
material_facts: The High Court dismissed the specific-performance suit after finding that the pleaded agreement had not been proved.
The Supreme Court found no basis to regard the High Court’s exercise of discretion as contrary to established principles or perverse.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court declined to interfere with the High Court’s decision, and dismissed the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20 of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 makes specific performance discretionary, while requiring that discretion to be sound, reasonable, and guided by judicial principles. The Court relied on Madamsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yellogi Rao and Sardar Singh v. Smt. Krishna Devi, and declined to exercise its jurisdiction under Article 136 of the Constitution of India.

predicates.appeal_challenging_refusal_of_specific_p: The proceeding was an appeal challenging a lower court’s refusal to grant specific performance.
predicates.lower_court_applied_judicial_principles: The lower court exercised its discretion by applying established judicial principles to the claim and evidence.
predicates.no_perverse_discretion: The lower court’s discretionary decision was not shown to be perverse.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a refusal of specific performance and the lower court applied judicial principles without exercising discretion perversely, appellate interference is not warranted.
